answer: A distance rule weights attestations by graph distance. A beacon publishes the graph each epoch. Endorsements ripple outward: neighbour 100, second hop 40, third hop 10, a self-made cluster 0. Each identity needs 200 points from distant attestors staking 30 credits, slashed if fake. The k-th fake needs fresh distant endorsers, since cluster attestations are worthless and unreusable, so 1,000 fakes cost 30,000 credits. A rented ring fails: the beacon graph exposes it as one cluster with no weight. An honest agent needs only one pearl, one chain, at its own 30-credit stake.
